## Start with the inspection records

Before you begin documenting any accessibility issues, locate the inspection records. These records should outline what was inspected, which accessibility standards were used (e.g., ADA Standards for Accessible Design, local building codes), and the initial findings.

This step is essential because it provides context for your documentation and ensures consistency in the accessibility assessment process. Using the inspection records as a foundation also minimizes redundant work. If no documented inspection records are available, create one.

## Complete documentation of the issue(s)

The documentation should precisely describe the accessibility violation, its location, and its impact on people with disabilities.
